    - `rounding` (trunc|round): shift and output rounding

    - `frac_guard` (0..4): extra fractional bits on x and y

  constraint: throughput_msps >= 32
  constraint: max_abs_err <= 0.000244141
  constraint: sys_p99_batch_us <= 0.5
  objective: min area_um2 (HV ref 100000)
  objective: max accuracy_bits (HV ref 12)
  select: min area_um2
  system (simulated at L2 for the shortlist; screened at L1 by an analytic bound): control loop: a tick every 1 us issues 32 requests at once (32 requests/us on average)
  budget: 400 evals, 100/round, <= 4 rounds, eps 0.01

Evaluation budget: 400 evaluations in total, up to 100 per round,
at most 4 rounds.

Propose the first exploration plan: which families to search (1-4) and the
parameter ranges for each, with a relative budget share. Prefer families that can
plausibly meet the constraints; spend the budget where the trade-offs are. Explain
your reasoning briefly in `rationale` and per family in `why`.

families.why: Only 1 result/cycle families can feed a 32-request burst inside 0.5 us; pipelined_m additionally cuts the number of register stages (ceil(N/m)+2) so it is the most likely area winner. The m sweep exposes the area-vs-Fmax trade-off: large m saves FFs but lengthens the combinational chain and the latency, which the batch bound punishes.

The full-register pipeline is the safest way to satisfy the burst deadline (latency N+2, one result/cycle, shortest combinational path so highest Fmax). It anchors the fast/high-margin end of the front and gives the accuracy/area boundary a reference point against pipelined_m.

A shared datapath would be far cheaper in area than any registered pipeline, so it is worth a cheap probe: with k=8 and N~13 it needs 32*(ceil(N/k)+3) ~ 160 cycles in 0.5 us, i.e. ~320 MHz, which is probably out of reach, but if it passes it dominates on area. Small share because the cycle count makes it a long shot.

parsed.rationale: The binding constraints are the burst deadline (32 results within 0.5 us of a 1 MHz tick) and max_abs_err <= 2^-12. Iterative is excluded analytically: 32*(N+3) cycles with N>=13 needs >1 GHz, and unrolled_k is only marginally better, so the front must come from the 1-result/cycle families. Accuracy needs roughly W>=14 (output LSB 2^-(W-2)) and N>=13 (residual angle ~2^-N), so I centre the boxes on W 13..18, N 12..18 with small guard ranges, and let the exact model find the true accuracy boundary. Area is the objective, so pipelined_m (fewer register stages) gets the largest share, with pipelined as the high-Fmax anchor and a small unrolled_k probe in case a shared datapath can still make the deadline. Later rounds should widen W/N upward for accuracy_bits > 12 (hypervolume) and map the full m/k ranges of whichever families survive.
